title: Field-arithmetic batch kernels
description:
Batched SIMD kernels for the field-arithmetic modules. The largest research-impact wins in the epic — extension-field tower ops have 3–6 independent base-field muls per element that schedule naturally onto SIMD lanes. ## Background Five field-arithmetic kernels lack batched SIMD. (1) GF($2^m$) for $m \in \{8, 16, 32\}$ is per-element scalar even though VPCLMULQDQ-on-YMM can process two element pairs per instruction. (2) GF($2^{571}$) — used for NIST B-571/K-571 EC research — is scalar multi-word with $9 \times 9$ word-pair XORs and shifts. (3) `Fp

` Montgomery batch is specialized only for `Fp<65537>` and `Fp<2^{31}-1>`; all other primes (including the 64-bit primes used by tower extensions) fall through to scalar. (4) `gfpn::QuadraticExt::mul` has 3 independent base-field muls per Karatsuba but no SoA layout. (5) `gfpn::CubicExt::mul` has 6. This story has five child tasks: C1 GF($2^m$) batch, C2 GF($2^{571}$) wide batch, C3 generic 64-bit Montgomery batch, C4 QuadraticExt SoA, C5 CubicExt SoA. C5 reuses C4's SoA scaffolding. C3 carries an explicit MSRV escalation gate: an AVX-512 IFMA52 sub-task may be opened only if AVX2 falls below $1.5\times$ and only after explicit user MSRV-bump approval per `escalation-policy.md`. ## Success Criteria - [hard] Each child task ships per the per-kernel execution protocol from the epic spec doc. - [hard] Existing Mersenne/Fermat specialisations and AoS paths remain unchanged and at least as fast. - [hard] Lean4 proofs still build (`./scripts/verify-lean.sh`) for any kernel touching `gfp/`. - [hard] No MSRV bump without explicit user approval — C3 IFMA52 sub-task opens only on demonstrated need. ## Notes Bench targets: `gf2m_mul_strategies`, `gf2m_wide_mul`, `fp_specialized`, `fieldvec_dot_product`, `field_matrix_fusion`, `field_matrix_gemm`. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
